capabilities: check CSV columns against adjacent JSON rule files
report errors by logical row, column, rule and value
write Markdown reports next to the source CSV
preview trim and default fixes and write corrected copies (Pro)
batch check up to 20 CSV files with saved rule sets (Pro)
extras: Freemium: core checks and Markdown reports are free; trim/default fix previews and batch checking require a $5/month or $15 one-time GitHub Sponsors payment, with sign-in via the GitHub device flow and offline Pro grace of 14 days. The README lists extensive untested areas (mobile, Linux, screen readers, sync conflicts, large vaults). The listing notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff, and the settings open a What's new tab promoting other NoteMods plugins.
problem: Obsidian stores CSV files but offers no way to validate their columns against rules before using or sharing the data.
